# Mods adversarial discovery

Status: independent discovery, 2026-10-08. These are proposed risks and acceptance tests, not adopted operator decisions or executed qualification. Ownership is limited to this report and adversarial/ captures. Original discovery-20261007, historical FAILs, consumed reservations, canonical assumptions and all implementation gates remain unchanged.

## Finding and trustworthy scope

Mods merit a bounded qualification lane for observing execution, shaping prompts, transforming streamed responses and serving controlled tools. A durability design must survive their absence or failure. Put effect authority in an independent preventive control which fails closed even when the observer or transformer is missing. Admission checks alone cannot close a failure that occurs after admission.

The [official announcement](https://claude.dev/blog/getting-started-with-claude-code-mods/) demonstrates observe, replace and hold patterns, session-local host state surviving hot reload, and runtime-backed plugin tests. It explicitly treats Blast Radius as a command-text safety net; substitutions, aliases and scripts escape that classifier. The published test kit can exercise hook behavior, but a mocked world beneath a mod does not prove actual process containment, durable storage acknowledgement or SDK recovery.

The [pinned declarations](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts) specify fallback on throw, budget exhaustion and invalid return: lower hooks/core run, or the last next result remains. Catch handlers have bounded grace and replay-safe next. Engine events identify agent loops separately from plugin origin. turn.step is streamed; outermost output is shown/recorded. Tool results pass native schema/mapping; returning a core object retains its opaque ref. Plugin-generated calls skip their calling hook frame. Direct mcp.call does not prompt. These capabilities do not specify a durable, externally accepted checkpoint or exact original SDK pending-result recovery. Locators: EngineEventOf 3239, CatchHandler/Caught 876, HookBudget 4218, Next 5230, ToolCallResult 9822, StreamNext 9514, TurnStepChunk 10393, TurnStepInput 10419, AgentLoop 156, tool.call 2570, mcp.call 2320.

The [Mods README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/README.md) limits loading to builds with function hooks enabled and warns that the early access API may change. Its tests have hooks beneath the mod answering the world; an unanswered call throws. Pinned and current-main README/type bytes matched at capture, as recorded in [capture-ledger.json](adversarial/capture-ledger.json). That equality supplies no installed-binary or SDK loading proof. The copied candidate retains selected recovery evidence SDK 0.2.162 / CLI 2.1.274, local lock 0.2.154 and minimum-lane refusal. No source discovery changes those dispositions.

There are distinct published surfaces: the announcement requires CLI 2.1.287 or later and uses $.state, while the pinned declaration header identifies 2.1.277 and its engine state noun is $.store. Do not combine these into a single tested API. Qualify the runtime-emitted declarations and actual behavior of the chosen build in the SDK subprocess. A new managed trusted Mod lane is separate from the current runner's plugins=[] and denial of arbitrary plugin Skills; discovery supplies no authority to loosen those controls.

The [sec-default source](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/sec-default/hooks/register.ts) and [README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/sec-default/README.md) supply an important scoped counterexample to blanket rejection: managed deny-rule holding and plugin-admission handlers deliberately recover conservatively. Its protection depends on exact seating, settings and policy. It does not add general policy or protect every engine event. Managed prependPlugins can omit it; user-tier loading cannot obtain the managed move. It passes process, filesystem, HTTP and MCP events. Thus organizational permission protection is useful, but cannot establish complete mediation of arbitrary plugin effects or external durability authority.

## Proposed oracle contract

These are experimental requirements derived from the candidate, not vendor guarantees. Every case records source/installed SDK/CLI/plugin hashes, tier/order/settings, lineage, original call identity, exact typed input/result, candidate receipt, accepted receipt identity and owner instance. Use a synthetic independent physical recorder outside all killed/restored domains. Its records count actual process launches, file mutations and accepted synthetic remote requests. Trace messages are diagnostic; their absence never proves zero effect.

For a held accepted ordinal define E as physical effect count, C as externally accepted receipt/result count, and R as replacement dispatch count. Safe refusal before intent requires E=0 and R=0. Known accepted outcome requires E=1, exactly one accepted identity, exact original result and valid postimages; a replacement may append that result but may not redispatch the effect. Postintent ambiguity requires E in {0,1}, R=0 and PARKED, with no fabricated unknown/error result advancing the model. Candidate receipt presence without accepted commit never authorizes effect. Any E>1, wrong-call result, unexpected model continuation or effect before accepted authority is FAIL. Losing previously acknowledged accepted state under a selected preservation contract is FAIL even if the system later parks.

Record native tool launches separately from authorized wrapper dispatches. A FAIL can occur without duplicate effects if a failed hook permits one unauthorized native launch. Add a synthetic provider request counter for model replacement tests; effect and model billing counts are different oracles. A second provider request may be allowed only for explicitly unaccepted computation, never presented as recovery of an accepted result.

Native mapper/ref evidence and exact stored JSON evidence are separate. A transformed native tool envelope must prove both the model-facing mapping and the original adapter's authoritative JSON/type equality. A matching UI string, joined result text or process-local ref cannot substitute for either proof.

## Adversarial matrix

All rows below are proposed tests. No row claims PASS. The failure expectations preserve the candidate's single serial original pending route; child/parallel support requires a separate qualification before admission.

| ID | Injection and risk | Exact effects, commit and replacement oracle | Control and qualification |
|---|---|---|---|
| MA-01 | Throw before next in a tool gate, including unavailable intent authority. Native fallback could run. | Recorder sees zero native launches and E=0, C unchanged, R=0; explicit refusal. A named hook error with one launch is FAIL. | Remove mod entirely as a mutation. Independent execution gate must still prevent effects. |
| MA-02 | Exhaust own-code budget before next; distinguish from long waiting inside engine calls. | Same as MA-01. Bound whole operation externally; timeout classification must not authorize takeover or native dispatch. | Hook time budget is not a lifecycle or storage deadline. |
| MA-03 | Return wrong schema, undefined, contradictory deny/result, or malformed typed tool output before next. | Validation/fallback may be observed, but no native launch or accepted fabricated result; E=0, C unchanged, R=0. | Validation alone is insufficient if the failure fallback reaches core. |
| MA-04 | Omit module/matcher, disable function hooks, import/register failure, policy refusal, wrong plugin name or headless route. | Startup admission refuses before effect/model request. If loss occurs after startup, independent guard still blocks; E=0. | Prove actual SDK subprocess mode loads exact required hooks, not merely plugin validate or terminal UI. |
| MA-05 | Catch answers deny; then catch itself throws, exceeds grace or misreturns. | Successful pre-next deny gives E=0. Catch failure still requires E=0 through independent control. | A local catch improves resilience but cannot be the only guard against its own failure. |
| MA-06 | next executes effect; hook crashes before recording outcome. Catch calls next again. | E=1, no second launch; missing exact durable outcome parks, R=0. Complete recorded outcome reconciles once against accepted dispatch. | Test replay-safe catch separately from crash recovery. Returning deny afterward cannot undo an effect. |
| MA-07 | Ordinary hook calls next twice or races two calls; two sibling hooks also attempt dispatch. | At most one intent/claim winner and E<=1. Loser refuses; no replacement/new ordinal escape. | Do not infer ordinary next is generally idempotent from catch replay semantics. |
| MA-08 | Plugin raises tool.call recursively; direct mcp.call/process.run/http.fetch/fs.write route avoids selected matcher. | Every unauthorized synthetic effect path yields E=0; allowed wrapper path E<=1 with matching intent. | Inventory all effect-producing engine calls, origins and credentials. Restrict capabilities independently. |
| MA-09 | Child, teammate, background agent and internal fork emit calls; agent listing is incomplete. | Unsupported child recovery refuses before E; parent cannot supply child result under its own identity. Native background descendants counted independently. | agentId versus origin is an identity dimension, not a supported recovery guarantee. |
| MA-10 | Parallel tool calls share mutable held state or complete out of order. | Selected serial lane rejects concurrency before E; no swapped original tool IDs/results. Future concurrent lane needs per-call isolated state and exact ordering proof. | UI single held variable is not a durability ledger. |
| MA-11 | Stream hook throws after text or partial tool JSON, then fallback continues; alter/drop/reorder chunks. | Capture exact emitted/recorded chunks, final tool identity and provider count. No effect from partial/duplicate tool call; accepted prefix remains identical on replacement. | Fault at each chunk boundary, including stop. Unaccepted computation can restart only under explicit policy. |
| MA-12 | Replace model response without next; crash before/after durable acceptance; retain opaque engine refs across restart. | No provider request for a successful fully synthetic response; no accepted result substitution. C=1 only after exact durable receipt. Replacement rejects stale refs or incompatible response. | Qualify complete response versus stream assembly; an opaque in-process handle is not a portable checkpoint. |
| MA-13 | Return core result by identity, then copied result, then hook-generated result; known errors and multimodal/MCP output. | Compare native model-facing transcript blocks and opaque stored entries, not joined text. Preserve false, 0, null, array order, isError and tool mapping. Reject incompatible type/schema before append. | Differential tests cover full output versus truncated/persisted representations. |
| MA-14 | Modify turn.complete display or UI while original transcript remains. | Display changes never alter accepted outcome, C or pending result. Replacement uses authoritative raw state, not screen text. | UI useful for explanation/inspection; cannot certify durable result replacement. |
| MA-15 | Compaction, prompt caches, resume and session-local state hide/remove observer history. | Accepted pending identity and unresolved intent survive independently. No new effect or ordinal from cache miss/state reset; R=0 for ambiguity. | Test cached hits as well as dispatches and failed invalidation. Session history API must not replace opaque SessionStore. |
| MA-16 | Reload module between admission, acceptance, intent and effect; dependency or type contract changes without version bump. | Source/package/chain mismatch refuses before next transition; no mutable accepted suffix. Previously accepted records bind original fingerprint. | Read-only package and immutable dependency closure; hash after load and at authority boundary, not manifest version alone. |
| MA-17 | User tool.check returns allow over deny; ask becomes allow; sec-default omitted or configured to override. | Forbidden synthetic route has E=0 across intended deployment matrix. Record which rule/seat held or failed. | Test managed policy as deployed. Permission bypass remains a capability requiring restriction, not a claim of universal secure defaults. |
| MA-18 | Kill at each intent ACK, claim ACK, effect start/completion, result ACK, accepted commit and conditional append gap. | Before acceptance E=0. Any ambiguous ACK reconciles same identity or parks. Known orphan outcome adopted only if exact input/result/postimages match; E<=1, no redispatch. | Enumerate both sides of every barrier, including hook fails after each write. |
| MA-19 | Restore workspace/claims to before intent while losing result; lose/regress independent intent authority. | Intact intent causes PARKED and R=0. Missing/regressed authority refuses unrecoverably. Never recreate empty authority, claims or lineage. | Snapshot rollback experiment stays required when Mods are present. |
| MA-20 | Old owner partitioned but still emitting; hook aborted while descendant or network request survives. | Replacement remains denied until independent terminal evidence; any new old-owner request after terminal receipt is FAIL. Predeath request accepted later remains ambiguous and parks. | next.signal and hook cancellation are cooperative; test whole environment containment. |
| MA-21 | Accepted result or envelope differs after package/CLI/SDK upgrade or replacement host. | Refuse before startup/append unless exact compatibility lane qualifies. No ordinary conversation resume or re-run to reconstruct accepted output. | Test required SDK loading and selected original pending adapter together; separate pin equality from behavior. |

## Necessary candidate edits for synthesis

These are recommendations, not modifications made by this lane.

1. Add a Mods capability boundary to spec Interfaces and plan Stack: an optional candidate integration through existing runner seams, with observed event/output scope and actual SDK loading qualification. Keep PolicyExecutorUnavailable until the authorized executor integration passes its gate.
2. In INV-5 ordered protocol, state that throwing, timing out, invalid output, missing hooks or catch failure must not permit native effects. Bind the independent effect gate and exact hook/package/chain admission to each authority transition. Do not change the accepted-before-effect order.
3. Extend M1 P2 with MA-01 through MA-14 offline transport/native-mapping cases and deliberate missing-gate mutations. A stubbed core success is a mapping/chain test, not physical zero-effect proof. Later rig tests need independently measured actual effects.
4. Extend M3 P6 with exact SDK subprocess Mods loading and native transcript/result differential evidence, if that route is chosen. No install, live execution or proof reservation is authorized by this report. Keep unsupported child/parallel paths refused.
5. Extend M4 P7/P9 with direct plugin engine effect routes, sec-default seating/policy combinations, dependency closure hashes, reload at barriers and compatibility refusal. Reuse P1/P3/P5 intent/rollback/termination oracles rather than weaken them because an engine hook exists.
6. Add source receipts for the official announcement, pinned declarations, README and sec-default. Retain historical FAIL and minimum-lane refusal; add any later qualified lane as new evidence with distinct source/version/runtime pins.

Open questions for the lead: which hooks the selected SDK headless subprocess actually loads; whether exact native tool result mapping aligns with the existing pending adapter; which independent control blocks native and direct plugin effects when the mod is absent; and whether the selected failure contract needs accepted model-response durability beyond the existing accepted pending boundary. No answer is inferred from publication or API declarations.
